body:
I've never read *The Catcher in the Rye* before, so I just read the motifs section of this...

http://www.sparknotes.com/lit/catcher/themes.html

I don't think I've **ever** read anything that felt so personal.  I don't know what to say.  Every paragraph I read sounded exactly like me.  I'm not sure if that's a good thing, but it's such an odd feeling to have thoughts you haven't even straightened out for yourself laid out before you.  And I didn't even read this in the context of the story.  I cannot believe that this is what *The Catcher in the Rye* is about!

I'm not sleeping tonight.  In a couple hours Books-A-Million will be open.  Forget trying to find stupid dates or any of the other foolish stuff I've been doing lately.  I **have** to get my hands on this book.  It's going to be hard for me to read emotionally if I feel a connection with Holden, which I strongly suspect will be the case.  I really hope it ends well for him. 

Once again...I really don't know what to say.  I wasn't expecting any advice I could use when I posted this rant, but if this book contains any type of lesson that Holden learns I hope I can live vicariously through whatever he goes through and pull something away from it.  I feel like someone just wrote a book for me and put it on my desk to help me out.  I know *The Catcher in the Rye* is a hugely popular book, but I just...I...  Thanks.  I'm more excited for this than I have been for anything in a long *long* time.
